Text-message notices are now cut to 160 characters: a longer body keeps its first 157 characters and ends in `...`. All 62 tests pass.

The change is in `lib/notices/compose.js`. Every notice goes through `composeNotice`, including the hold-ready notice and the morning digest, so one change covers them all. Email notices are not touched, and a text of 160 characters or fewer is left as it is.

I added two tests to `test/notices.test.js`. One checks that a long-title hold notice by text comes out at exactly 160 characters ending in `...`, while the same notice by email stays in full. The other checks that a short text is unchanged.

One shell command I ran to append the tests was blocked, so I added them with the Edit tool instead. That command had not changed any file.

My first version of the long-title test had a wrong assertion. It compared the first 157 characters of the text and the email, which differ because Ben and Ada are greeted by different names. I fixed the assertion, not the code.

The cut counts JavaScript string characters, not bytes. If your provider counts a message with emoji or accented titles differently, those could still be rejected.
